column1: # PSEUDOCODE THAT WAS TRANSCRIBED AND RUN, AND WHAT THE RUN MEASURED.
# WHAT THIS CHANNEL PROVES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.
# This skill's headline caveat is that citations are ATTRIBUTED, not verified: check.py proves
# a claim points at a real entry with a locator, never that the cited paper says what the
# document claims. Executing a pseudocode block is a THIRD thing, narrower than either:
#   check.py green     -> the citation is well-formed.
#   a row here         -> the block, transcribed literally, produces the number printed beside
#                         it. The block is self-consistent and implementable.
#   `verified:` header -> a human read the cited work. NO GAIA DOCUMENT CARRIES THIS.
# A green row here does NOT mean the algorithm is the one in the cited paper. A block can run
# perfectly and still be attributed to the wrong source -- the clipmap and Bruneton-Fresnel
# defects in source-findings.tsv were both exactly that. Do not let this file be read as
# verification of provenance.
# WHY IT EXISTS. Four of the nine severe/high defects found in the 2026-09-02 review were
# invisible to reading and only appeared on execution: a NaN that scalar Python `min` hides
# and GPU `min` propagates, a droplet loop that never writes the variable it reads, a talus
# artefact whose axis was stated backwards, and a pass count wrong by 10x. Reading found none
# of them. An unrun block is an unverified block, and this file is the record of which is which.
# PROVENANCE COLUMN. `lead` = re-executed by the person recording the row, against the current tree, numbers
# below are that run's. `agent` = measured by the reviewing agent and recorded on its report,
# NOT independently re-run. The distinction is the same one the skill makes everywhere else,
# and rows are not promoted from agent to lead without an actual second run.
# TERMINATION COLUMN (added 2026-09-07, PLAN success criterion 2 / audit X1b). A row here says a
# block reproduces a NUMBER. Until this column existed it never said the block STOPS, and the two
# are not the same claim. heightfield-raymarching.md's row is why: it measured missed hits, went
# green as SOUND, and the same block livelocked on 35.7% of 600 rays and 72.5% past 5 km -- found
# by hand a fortnight later, not by that run. SKILL.md:103 now reads "soundness is not
# termination" because of it. This column makes that distinction structural instead of remembered.
# THE VALUE DESCRIBES THE BLOCK AS PRINTED IN THE DOCUMENT, NEVER THE HARNESS THAT RAN IT. A
# harness that wraps a fenced expression in 400 timesteps says nothing about the fence; a driver
# loop living in prose beside the fence is not part of the block, and the cell says so when it
# matters. Vocabulary, narrowest first:
#   n/a            the block is code and contains no loop, no recursion, no back-edge: closed
#                  forms, straight-line assignments, a Sigma or a comprehension over a stated
#                  finite index set. It cannot fail to halt. Settled by READING the fence.
#   halts-proven   every loop is over a statically finite set, or the cell carries a termination
#                  ARGUMENT a reader can re-check against the printed block in one sitting. An
#                  argument, not a run -- and it is only worth the precondition it names.
#   halts-measured a data-dependent loop (while / until-tolerance / worklist) that a RECORDED run
#                  drove to completion with the cap not reached. Says nothing about inputs outside
#                  that run, which is exactly what the raymarching row taught.
#   cap-bounded    only a step or iteration cap stops it; remove the cap and it can spin.
#   unknown        never examined for termination. The honest default: a row is NOT promoted out
#                  of `unknown` by a run that measured some other property.
#   no-block       the row registers a prose claim, a table, a cost estimate or a cross-document
#                  measurement -- not a fenced block. There is nothing to run, so termination does
#                  not apply. This is the value that says criterion 2 has nothing to hold here.
# The first whitespace-delimited token is the value; anything after it is a note, the way the
# provenance column already carries its warnings. check.py fails a row with the wrong field count
# or a token outside that list, and REPORTS the `unknown` count.
# HOW A CELL NAMES ANOTHER ROW: by document and block, NEVER by line number. A `:NN` anywhere in
# this file is a line in a REFERENCE DOCUMENT; a row has no stable line of its own, because every
# row that lands above it moves it. This column's own edit is the proof. It inserted 55 lines of
# header above the data, and the seven cells written as `row :NN` kept their old NN -- which now
# lands inside this comment block instead of on the row each one meant, and no guard said a word.
# check.py now FAILS the register on `row :` or `rows :` followed by a number, so the idiom is
# enforced and not merely recommended. TWO THINGS THAT GUARD CANNOT DO. ⚠️ It does not see
# POSITIONAL prose -- one cell below still says "the row above", which breaks the same way the
# moment a row lands between them, and it survives here only because it is an original cell and
# not this edit's to rewrite. ⚠️ It does not resolve the `:NN` references INTO reference
# documents: those files are edited by other hands, an insertion anywhere above a fence silently
# moves it, and doing so would put a guard in this repo permanently red on other people's work.
# Where the owning document is under repair right now, the cells below name the fence by its
# CONTENT and give no line at all -- a description does not go stale.
# THE 2026-09-07 AUDIT, AND WHAT IT DID NOT DO. All 73 rows were classified by reading the fenced
# block each row names. NO BLOCK WAS RE-EXECUTED FOR THIS COLUMN. `halts-measured` was written
# only where the row's own recorded numbers require the loop to have finished -- pass counts to a
# tolerance, a fixed point reached, 0/600 with the cap unhit -- and no row was upgraded on
# evidence this pass did not hold. Result: 30 n/a, 20 no-block, 15 halts-proven, 8 halts-measured,
# and `unknown` and `cap-bounded` are empty. That is not a clean bill of health, it is where the
# risk actually sits: 20 of 73 rows register no block at all, and this file cannot see the other
# half of criterion 2. ⚠️ THE GAP COUNTS IN THIS PARAGRAPH AND THE NEXT ARE AS OF 2026-09-07 AND
# WERE CLOSED ON 2026-09-08 -- see THE 2026-09-08 FENCE ENUMERATION below. They are kept, not
# rewritten, because what the audit could and could not see is the record. As found then:
# 107 fenced blocks across the 37 files of references/ today, of which 11
# files holding 20 fences appear in no row here (caustics, gpu-driven-culling, node-graph-runtime,
# resolution-independence, shader-craft, simulation-time-budget, tiled-streaming,
# water-closed-vs-open, plus the coverage/papers format templates). check.py prints 103 / 34 / 8
# for those same three counts and is NOT disagreeing: it excludes papers*.md, index.md and
# coverage.md, whose four fences are `- **id** `T` — Author (Year).` templates and not code. Both
# sets are as of 2026-09-07; the guard's are recomputed every run and these are not, so believe
# the guard if they ever part.
# The per-FENCE gap is larger still and NOTHING can count it mechanically, because rows are keyed
# by prose and not by line: a row may cover several fences and several rows one fence. Counted by
# hand on 2026-09-07 it is about 33 further fences inside documents that DO have rows, under the
# criterion NO ROW RAN THIS FENCE -- which is STRICTER than the mechanical count above, where a
# document counts as registered the moment its name appears in the document column. The two
# criteria disagree, and the hand count uses the strict one: river-networks.md's carve fence is
# NAMED by the carving row and still counts here, because that row says in as many words that
# what it measured was the prose running minimum and not that fence. Ten of the 33 are in
# water-optics.md alone, where the unpolarised-Fresnel row covers three of thirteen. Two are the
# loops this column would most want and cannot reach: heightfield-lod.md:73's
# `refine while rho > tau` and mesh-extraction.md's `while not done`, neither of which prints a
# stopping rule.
# THE 2026-09-08 FENCE ENUMERATION (criterion 2's second half). Every fenced block in references/
# was enumerated mechanically and then matched to rows BY HAND under the strict criterion -- a row
# RAN this fence, not a row mentions it. Denominators, so the numbers can be re-derived: 107 fences
# in 37 files, 103 in the 34 files check.py scores (papers*.md, index.md and coverage.md hold the
# other 4, and they are entry-format templates). Of those 103, 55 had been run by an existing row
# and 48 had not: 16 in the 8 documents that held a fence and no row at all, and 32 inside
# documents that DO have rows. That 32 is the hand count the paragraph above put at "about 33" and
# is the closest thing to independent corroboration this criterion has -- two hands, a day apart,
# one fence apart. 48 rows were added, one per unregistered fence, so check.py's document-level
# gap is now 0 and every one of those 103 is named by a row. The remaining 4 are named by no row
# and are meant not to be: 2 in papers-flow.md, 1 each in papers-generation.md and coverage.md,
# all four entry-format templates, and none of those three files appears in the document column.
# WHAT THOSE 48 ROWS ARE AND ARE NOT. 28 were transcribed and RUN; 20 were READ and not run, and
# every one of those says NOT RUN in its provenance cell and NOT MEASURED in its outcome. Grep the
# provenance column for `RUN 2026-09-08` and `NOT RUN` and the two sets come out 28 and 20. Three
# of the 28 are only partly run and say so in their own outcome cell rather than here: the
# virtual-texture gradient scale (its arithmetic, never a shader), the absorption samples (the
# printed 141x ratio, never the spectrum) and knickpoint celerity (an exponent identity checked
# symbolically, which produces no numbers because it needs none). A row
# that says NOT MEASURED is worth having -- it converts an unexamined fence into an examined one
# with a known status -- but it is NOT evidence about the block, and nothing here should be read
# as promoting a fence from unrun to verified. The termination values are 44 n/a, 3 halts-proven
# and 1 unknown; `n/a` is settled by READING, which this column has always allowed, and no row was
# written `halts-measured` on a block this pass did not execute.
# THE TRAP THIS PASS EXISTS TO CATCH, FOUND TWICE MORE. The header's worked example is
# river-networks.md's carve fence, named by the carving row and not run by it. Two more of the same
# shape turned up: hydraulic-erosion.md's multi-class capacity fence, named in the per-class repose
# row's termination cell while that row measured a slippage relaxation; and sea-ice.md's free-drift
# law, named in the floe-size row's termination cell while that row measured a Voronoi partition.
# Both now have rows that ran them. This is why the mechanical count is a FLOOR: all three fences
# sat in documents the document column already listed.
# THREE THINGS THIS PASS CHANGED ABOVE. (1) mesh-extraction.md's `while not done` is no longer
# unreachable: its row carries a termination argument -- each iteration consumes one unused grid
# point, so the trip count is bounded by N whatever `done` is -- and that argument, not a run, is
# what makes it halts-proven. The paragraph above is left as written; treat this as its erratum.
# (2) heightfield-lod.md's `refine while rho > tau` IS still unreachable and is now the register's
# only `unknown`. The count rising from 0 to 1 is the guard working, not a regression: it was 0
# because nobody had looked, and it is 1 because someone did and could not settle it.
# (3) mask-operators.md's signed-distance fence was run for the first time and the caution printed
# beside it does not hold -- see that row. NOT FIXED HERE: this register's owner does not edit
# reference documents.

column4: Burt-Adelson 5-tap a=0.4, separable, L=5, 256^2, EXPAND normalised by 4. Round-trip exactness reproduces in every row (1.4e-14 to 2.3e-13 m). The MAGNITUDES DO NOT. On smoothed noise: reflect/reflect -0.15%, reflect/symmetric +0.02%, reflect/edge +2.22%, reflect/zero -15.01%, zero/reflect -9.94%. Across four surfaces the same pairs range -15.0% to +2.2% (noise), -1.0% to -11.2% (full-width ramp AND corner wedge, all negative), +0.0% to +1.1% (offset plateau). Nothing reached +27.6% or +36.8% on any field tried, and the sign is field-dependent.
column5: MECHANISM CONFIRMED, NUMBERS REJECTED. The parity argument holds -- EXPAND pads a zero-interleaved array, and only reflect preserves the even/odd lattice -- and the structural point stands: round-trip exactness is blind to low-band volume error. But the reported figures do not reproduce, and on smoothed noise 'symmetric' measured SMALLER than 'reflect', contradicting the document's own 'reflect, and only reflect'. Table replaced with the measured spread, the field-dependence stated as the finding, and the pad-mode choice re-argued from parity rather than from a measured win. *** THIS REJECTION WAS ITSELF TOO NARROW, corrected 2026-09-04. It was measured at 256^2 ONLY. The rejected magnitudes REPRODUCE ON AN ODD GRID: at N = 257 the same configuration gives +28.4% (symmetric) and +37.9% (edge) on fBm, against the reported +27.6% and +36.8%. The effect is a PARITY effect in N, not a property of the field -- holding the field fixed and varying only N, reflect/edge moves from +1.8% at 256 to +34.1% at 257 -- and Burt & Adelson p. 534 defines EXPAND as taking an (M+1)x(N+1) array to a (2M+1)x(2N+1) one, so every level of a canonical pyramid is ODD by construction and 257 is the representative case, not 256. So the original report was right and this row rejected it for testing the one grid size where the effect vanishes. Recorded rather than rewritten: a register that rejects a true finding is the same defect as one that accepts a false one.

column2: does the document's own prescribed fix for the missing mesa tread actually work?
column3: its recommendation to 'run thermal after the layered hydraulic pass with a per-bed talus angle', offered as the fix for its headline negative result
column4: Synthetic butte, 192^2 at 50 m cells: a 400 m escarpment, 100 m beds, resistant talus 60 deg and weak 32 deg, relaxed to convergence. Talus limit ALONE moved the escarpment from 1.998 km to 1.996 km -- 2 m on a 2 km butte -- and area_hard went 49.61% to 48.91% against single-angle controls at 49.46% (32 deg), 49.52% (45 deg) and 49.62% (60 deg), i.e. per-bed angles are indistinguishable from one angle on that measure. Mass conserved to 1.6e-14%. Adding a weathering term on steep faces and CONTROLLING FOR TOTAL MASS REMOVED: uniform weathering destroys the landform (tread std 1.01 to 7.21 m, tread mean 500.02 to 151.01 m); bed-selective weathering gives textbook parallel retreat, scarp 1.998 to 1.360 km with the tread unchanged at std 1.01 and mean 500.02.
column5: THE PRESCRIPTION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. A slope limit only moves material where the slope exceeds it, so once the face sits at the limit the pass converges and nothing is undermined; retreat needs a REMOVAL term, and the per-bed quantity that matters is the weathering rate, not the talus angle. The talus angle makes the debris apron; the rate makes the landform. The critic reported sqrt(68)=8.246 against a truth of 10 for a cell at x=60. I 'corrected' that to 7.071, on the grounds that q=55 yields 50 -- but q=55 is 5 cells from the curve and is only seeded if the band is 5 wide.
